title: Adjusting withdrawals: guardrails
objectives: Apply the four guardrails to rate rises, falls, good years and big expenses.
Explain why flexible spending is so powerful.
body_md:
Adjusting withdrawals: simple guardrails (illustrative).

| If… | Then consider… |
| --- | --- |
| The withdrawal rate has risen well above the starting rate (e.g. corpus fell) | Skip the inflation increase this year, or trim extras |
| Markets fell sharply | Draw from Bucket 2, not equity; avoid selling growth assets low |
| The withdrawal rate has fallen well below the starting rate (good years) | A modest extra increase is possible |
| A big unplanned expense came up | Fund it from its own pot or Bucket 2, and rebuild over time |

Flexible spending in bad years is one of the most powerful ways to make a corpus last.
example: Corpus fell, rate rose well above the starting rate: skip the inflation increase this year, or trim extras. Markets fell sharply: draw from Bucket 2, not equity.
say: Skip the inflation increase when the rate has risen well above the starting rate.
After a sharp fall, draw from Bucket 2, not equity.
never: Always increase the SWP for inflation.
Sell growth assets low in a fall.

check.q: After a sharp market fall, the plan should usually…
check.why: Draw from Bucket 2. Give equity time to recover.

check.q: Can skipping the inflation increase after a bad year help money last?
o: Yes — flexible spending is a powerful guardrail
check.why: Flexible spending is a powerful guardrail.

check.q: If the withdrawal rate has fallen well below the starting rate (good years), consider:
check.why: The withdrawal rate has fallen well below the starting rate (good years): a modest extra increase is possible.
